summary: This benchmark evaluates whether a causal 25-dimensional subspace edit at an earlier Python class declaration can mediate its effect through isolated single-token pathways (the assignment tokens or the final query token) across layers 11–17 in Qwen2.5-14B. The author rigorously demonstrates that while the unrestricted intervention achieves high reversal rates (242/256 and 246/256), restricting the signal entirely to any single tested relay token abolishes the behavioral reversal (0/256), despite non-zero state displacement at those relays.
strengths: Rigorous, well-controlled experimental isolation comparing native baseline, unrestricted subspace intervention, and single-token relay bottleneck conditions.
Precise specification of the subspace estimation protocol, including ridge regression parameters, singular value cutoff, and paired reversal criteria.
Exemplary reproducibility documentation, including the exact Qwen2.5-14B commit hash, runtime environment (MLX, Python, NumPy), prompt generation templates, and execution time.
Transparent reporting of negative results alongside quantitative displacement metrics showing information reached the candidate tokens but failed to propagate the causal effect.
weaknesses: Narrow empirical scope limited to a single model architecture and size (Qwen2.5-14B) and a single intermediate layer boundary (block 17).
Focuses exclusively on individual single-token relays without evaluating multi-token sets or multi-head attention routing combinations that often characterize distributed circuits.
Framed as a benchmark, but primarily functions as an activation-patching mechanistic interpretability case study on synthetic Python prompts.
suggestions: Extend the bottleneck analysis across multiple layer exit boundaries (e.g., blocks 12, 14, 20) to map where the multi-token distribution of information diverges or reconverges.
Test multi-token combination relays (e.g., joint assignment sign and identifier tokens) to identify the minimal sufficient set of tokens needed to preserve the reversal effect.
Evaluate whether similar pathway bottlenecks hold on other open-weight models of comparable size (e.g., Llama 3 8B/70B) to determine if this routing behavior is model-specific.

claims.text: The underlying interchange method corresponds to the distributed alignment search and causal abstraction framework described in arXiv:2303.02536.
In distributed alignment search and causal interchange interventions, an orthonormal basis U is used to interchange linear subspaces between base and source activations x + UUᵀ(x_partner − x).

novelty_vs_existing.title: Finding Alignments Between Interpretable Causal Variables and Distributed Neural Representations
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Applies subspace interchange intervention techniques to evaluate specific intermediate token routing bottlenecks across multi-layer blocks (layers 11–17) in Qwen2.5-14B on paired Python identifier binding tasks.
